blockers:
claim: API contract violation: The header removes SignalListModel and its associated properties (signalModel, signalBatchCount) but the QML file was deleted that depended on these. The remaining QML/Main.qml references QtTune.signalModel which will no longer exist after this change, creating a broken API.; file: app/qml/Main.qml; quote: text: qsTr("frames:%1 notify:%2 drop:%3")
                .arg(QtTune.frameCount)
                .arg(QtTune.guiNotifyCount)
                .arg(QtTune.droppedFrames)
questions: What is the intended purpose of removing SignalListModel and signal decoding? The LiveViewPage QML is deleted, but the signal model properties are removed from the bridge without clear replacement.
How should the QML layer access signal data now that SignalListModel is removed? The LiveViewPage that used QtTune.signalModel is deleted, but no alternative is provided.
Is the backpressure mechanism truly intended to be removed? The original code had careful comments about bounding the queued backlog.
What replaces the signal batching/coalescing functionality? The commit title mentions 'coalesced signal updates' but the implementation removes the batching mechanism.

claim: C ABI integrity violation: The file includes 'qttune/signals.h' which provides signal decoding functions, but the code no longer includes this header after the removal of signal decoding logic. The remaining code still references qttune_decode_signal if it were to be used, and the signal-related types like QttuneSignalSet are still needed for the core functionality.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: #include "qttune/signals.h"

claim: Thread safety violation: The code removes the in-flight frame counting mechanism (m_inFlightFrames and MaxInFlightFrames) that was used for backpressure to prevent queue overflow. The comment in the original code explicitly mentions 'Backpressure: bound the QUEUED backlog'. Without this protection, frames could queue indefinitely in the Qt event loop.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: self->m_droppedFrames.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
